trickyParts: A retry that does not clear its attempt-cache entry is swallowed by the listener's own attempt dedupe (delivery.go), so the redelivery never reaches the session. TestUnplaceableAgentDeliveryRetriesThenGivesUp asserts the absence of the 'listener attempt-dedupe skip' line for exactly that reason.

JetStream stops redelivering at max_deliver silently - nothing in this repository consumes its advisory - so the listener must write its give-up record first. unplaceableMaxDeliveries is consumerMaxDeliver - 2, and TestUnplaceableRetryWindowFitsTheBoundsItDependsOn pins both that and the window staying inside the attempt cache's TTL.

A session read that did not answer is not evidence of absence, and the delivery path must not give a message up on it. It leaves no entry, so HandleAgentMessage reports ReasonNoSessionRecord for it, which already holds the retry open - the explicit flag the first draft carried was provably redundant and was removed in the simplify pass.
bus.ErrTooLarge and bus.ErrInvalidSubject both satisfy errors.Is(err, bus.ErrRefused), so one guard in writeBusUnavailable keeps Retry-After off the 413 and the 400 and on nothing else.

A send cannot reach bus.ErrInvalidSubject: its subject is built from target_session, and a target that would make an invalid subject is refused by the session bucket first, so the route answers 404 before the bus sees it. The 400 is therefore asserted through the publish route, which takes its topic as written.

The reviewer's round-two findings 5 and 6 together moved behaviour, not only words: a push that failed on the wire is now retried inside the window under session.ReasonPushFailed and counted unplaceable_push_failed, where it was given up on its first delivery and counted unplaceable_no_push_target. unplaceable_no_push_target now covers a record naming nothing to push to and a session another listener owns (ErrWrongMachine), which has no producer in production code today.

A deferred message holds one of the durable's 256 MaxAckPending slots for its whole window. unplaceableDeferralCap (64) bounds how many this handler holds at once; the counter is this process's own bookkeeping and is wrong in two directions no accounting can fix (a restart forgets its deferrals; a redelivery this handler never deferred releases a slot it never took), both of which under-count and are absorbed by the cap's distance from the budget.

The unreachable-path hunt the architect asked for turned up two more claims beside the ErrWrongMachine one: HandleAgentResult.Reason's doc said the NAKing interest path's Reason is read by the caller, which reads it only in the error-free branch that path never reaches (the assignment is set and never read, and was left in place since removing it is a code change in internal/session); and 'a push that failed on the wire is ReasonPushFailed' was incomplete, since prompt returns an error for any non-204 answer too. internal/session/session.go's own 'ErrWrongMachine is returned when a session belongs to a different machine' predates this pull request and was left alone.
